sections.h2: Webster County Recorder of Deeds: location and contact
sections.html:
The Recorder of Deeds works from Room 16 of the Webster County Courthouse in Marshfield. The office's street address is 101 N Crittenden, the mailing address is P.O. Box 546, Marshfield, MO 65706, and the phone is 417-859-5882. Email goes to recorder@webstercountymo.gov. Call before you mail anything or drive in, so you have the right street and the right fee.

The office aims to record and preserve land records accurately and quickly. It also issues marriage licenses and records and copies military discharge papers (DD-214).

The present courthouse, faced in Carthage marble, was built from 1939 to 1941 and is the county's third.

A standard document costs $26 for page one and $3 for every page after that. Documents that miss the format rules carry a $25 penalty on top, and copies of recorded documents are $1.00 per page.

Missouri raised recorder fees by a flat $2.00 on August 28, 2026 under Senate Bill 938. Call the Recorder for the current total on your deed before you send payment.

Three layout standards apply: a three inch margin at the top of the first page, three-quarters of an inch on the remaining sides, and letter-size white paper. A deed outside those lines is treated as non-standard and costs the extra $25.

State law adds content rules. Under RSMo 59.330, a deed has to carry a legal description of the land and a mailing address for one grantee, and the Recorder may not file it without them. Closing agents normally prepare the deed with these items in place. A seller who writes a deed without a title company should check every item before mailing it.

The online document search went live on February 1, 2023. The site is titled Document Search for the Index of Recorded Deeds. You register as a new user, and the account can then search and buy copies of recorded documents. Subscription levels run from free to several paid options, depending on use.

Searching in person at the Recorder's office in Room 16 is free. The paid online plan is $200 per month, with a limit of 300 documents viewed or printed. An owner checking a single deed can start with the free route.

The office also points owners to DeedWatch.com, a free service.

Marriage licenses are a regular part of the counter work. Both parties must appear with valid government identification, and each person has to supply a Social Security number and the month and year any prior marriage ended. An online application is optional and speeds things up.

  • License fee: $53, cash only.
  • Certified copy: $9, the document used to change a name on a driver's license or Social Security card.
  • Validity: 30 days, and the ceremony must take place in Missouri.

The office also records and issues copies of DD-214 military discharge papers.

sections.h2: Courthouse offices involved in a home sale
sections.html:
A sale touches several offices inside the same courthouse.

  • Recorder, Room 16: holds the deed, 417-859-5882.
  • Assessor, Room 19: values the parcel, 417-859-2169.
  • Collector, Room 15: bills and receives the tax, 417-859-2683.
  • County Clerk, Room 12: takes senior tax credit applications.

If you owe tax, two Collector rules matter. Delinquent years must be paid before the current year is accepted, and a statement is due on receipt and delinquent after December 31. A payment mailed on or before that day is on time if it carries a postmark.

sections.h2: How a deed moves from closing to the record
sections.html:
Most sales go through a title company, which prepares the deed and files it. If you handle the paperwork yourself, work in this order. First, confirm the legal description and the grantee's mailing address. Second, check the margins and paper size. Third, call the Recorder for the total fee on your page count. Fourth, mail or deliver the deed with payment to Room 16.

After the deed is recorded, the Assessor can update the parcel and the Collector can send future bills to the new owner. Ask the title company or the Recorder to confirm the recording date, and keep a copy with your closing papers. A cash sale has no lender waiting on the recorded deed, but the same layout, content and fee rules apply.

Visiting in person is the fastest way to find out whether a deed will be accepted. Bring the original signed deed, a clear legal description of the land and a mailing address for the grantee. Expect to pay the recording fee at the counter, so ask ahead about the total and the payment types the office takes. Marriage license fees are cash only.

If you only need a copy of something already recorded, look the document up first. Searching in the office costs nothing, and a copy runs $1.00 per page. For several documents, the online subscription may be cheaper than paying per page, but only if you will view or print a large number each month.

Owners who inherit a house or take over a family property often find an older deed that was never recorded. Take that deed to the Recorder before you list the house. Buyers and title companies want the record to show a clear chain of owners, and an unrecorded deed can hold up a closing.

Webster County had an estimated 43,054 residents on July 1, 2025, up 10.1 percent from the April 2020 base of 39,087. The county counted 15,847 housing units, and owners occupy 77.4 percent of homes.

For 2020 to 2024 the median owned home was worth $228,800. Typical monthly owner cost was $1,377 for those who carry a mortgage and $430 for those who do not. Median gross rent was $789. Building permits numbered 226 in 2025.

Webster County lies in the Springfield metropolitan area. The cities are Fordland, Marshfield, Niangua, Rogersville, Seymour and Strafford, and the one village is Diggins.

Public school districts include Fordland R-III, Logan-Rogersville R-VIII, Marshfield R-I, Niangua R-V and Seymour R-II. Students in some parts of the county attend Strafford and Fair Grove schools in Greene County or Conway in Laclede County. A property's district name appears on its tax statement and affects the rate.

faqs.q: What is the Webster County Recorder's phone number?
faqs.a: 417-859-5882. The office is in Room 16 of the courthouse in Marshfield and also takes email at recorder@webstercountymo.gov.

faqs.q: How much is the first page of a deed in Webster County?
faqs.a: $26 for the first page and $3 for each additional page. A non-standard document adds $25. Call to confirm the total after the 2026 statewide $2 increase.

faqs.q: Is the Webster County online records search free?
faqs.a: There is a free level after registration, and in-office search in Room 16 is free. A paid plan costs $200 per month for 300 documents viewed or printed.

faqs.q: What margins does a Webster County deed need?
faqs.a: Three inches at the top of page one and three-quarters of an inch on the other sides, on 8.5 by 11 white paper.

faqs.q: How long is a Webster County marriage license valid?
faqs.a: Thirty days, and it must be used in Missouri. The license costs $53 in cash, and a certified copy is $9.
